title: Standard 12-Hour Clock
intro: The conventional 12-hour clock presents local civil time as two half-day periods, AM and PM.
structure: Hours run from 1 to 12, with minutes and seconds from 00 to 59. Midnight starts the AM period at 12:00; noon starts the PM period at 12:00. The period marker disambiguates otherwise identical readings.
example: 00:00 is 12:00 AM; 12:00 is 12:00 PM; 18:45:09 is 6:45:09 PM. Hiding seconds gives 6:45 PM.
history: The division of the day into two sets of twelve hours predates modern digital clocks. This provider implements the present-day civil convention rather than unequal seasonal hours.
model: The provider divides the supplied local day phase into ordinary seconds, converts the hour modulo 12 (mapping zero to 12), and selects AM before noon and PM from noon onward. Japanese and Chinese markers precede the number; other supported libc locale markers follow it, with AM/PM as fallback. It updates at the next second or minute boundary, rounded up to milliseconds.
limits: Uses the supplied civil UTC offset; no historical local clock standards or geographic coordinates are reconstructed. Explicit 12-hour selection is distinct from the operating system's locale-following standard mode.
